songInfo.title: Time
songInfo.album: The Dark Side of the Moon

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: F# Dorian Verse to A Major Chorus

scalesUsed.application: David Gilmour's legendary fuzz-laden guitar solo

scalesUsed.notes: F# - G# - A - B - C# - D# - E
scalesUsed.application: The cyclical verse groove balancing F#m and major IV (B) with the raised 6th (D#)

scalesUsed.notes: F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E
scalesUsed.application: The lyrical Dmaj7 to Amaj7 chorus progression

mainProgression.description: Hypnotic Dorian verse groove followed by lush major seventh chord expansions in the chorus

sectionProgressions.description: Ticking clocks and pulsing rototom percussion over a deep minor funk groove
Stately minor cadence expressing existential reflection ('Ticking away the moments that make up a dull day')

sectionProgressions.progression: Dmaj7 - Amaj7 - Dmaj7 - Amaj7 - C#m - Bm - E
sectionProgressions.description: Lush major-7th release transitioning into the minor circle turnaround

sectionProgressions.progression: F#m - Bm - F#m - Bm - Dmaj7 - C#m - Bm - E
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - iv - i - iv - ♭VI - v - iv - ♭VII
sectionProgressions.description: Epic canvas for David Gilmour's singing fuzz-faced bends and multi-delay textures

harmonicFunction: F#m tonic grounds the song in heavy existential contemplation
Dmaj7 (♭VI) in the chorus introduces breathtaking harmonic expansion with its raised C# major-seventh interval
The shift from F# minor to relative A major mirrors the illusion of time slipping through one's fingers
The F# Dorian IV chord (B major) injects momentary melodic brightness before resolving to dark minor

techniques.name: High-Sustain Fuzz & Wide Vocal Vibrato
techniques.description: Gilmour's signature Stratocaster lead tone using Silicon Fuzz Face, tape echo, and singing finger vibrato

notes: Utilizes a Dallas Arbiter Silicon Fuzz Face into a Hiwatt DR103 100W tube head
Wide, controlled finger vibrato executed from the wrist, shaking notes in perfect pitch modulation
Multi-tap tape echoes (Binson Echorec) expand single notes into soaring cavernous soundscapes
sequence: Pick 11th fret G string with heavy downstroke
Execute full 1.5-step bend up to E
Sustain note through fuzz compression and add slow, wide vibrato at peak
tips: Support the bending ring finger with your index and middle fingers
Do not rush the vibrato; let the natural bloom of the tube amplifier sustain the note

techniques.name: Lush Major 7th Chord Voicings
techniques.description: Voicing open and movable Dmaj7 and Amaj7 grips with ringing high strings

notes: Dmaj7 voiced as X-X-0-2-2-2 or 5th-fret barre
Amaj7 voiced as X-0-2-1-2-0 with the open A bass note
Clean Fender-style rhythm tone with gentle rotary / Uni-Vibe modulation
sequence: Strum Dmaj7 on beat 1 with light pick attack
Let the major 7th note (C#) chime against the D root
Slide smoothly into the Amaj7 shape on beat 3
tips: Keep fingers arched high to avoid muting the ringing high E string
Use a thin or medium pick for smooth acoustic-like strumming consistency

sections.name: Verse Groove
sections.description: The heavy, deliberate march of the verse with Nick Mason's snare and Richard Wright's electric piano.
notes: Accentuate the downbeats with percussive authority
Let the high notes of the F#m barre chord ring through
Tight rhythm locking with the kick drum

sections.name: Chorus (Tired of Lying)
sections.description: Soaring, melancholic vocal release with lush backing vocal choir and shimmering major 7th chords.
sections.progression: Dmaj7 - Amaj7 - Dmaj7 - Amaj7 - C#m - Bm - E
notes: Gentle strumming allowing the rich chord extensions to bloom
Smooth voice-leading between Dmaj7 and Amaj7
Build dynamic intensity leading into the C#m turnaround

sections.name: David Gilmour Guitar Solo
sections.description: Widely regarded as one of the greatest guitar solos ever recorded, packed with vocal bends and singing sustain.
sections.progression: F#m - Bm - F#m - Bm - Dmaj7 - C#m - Bm - E
notes: Fuzz Face into cranked Hiwatt with tape echo delay
Execute dramatic 1.5-step over-bends on the G and B strings
Vocal-like wrist vibrato on every held note

guitar.recommended: Fender Custom Shop David Gilmour Signature Stratocaster ('The Black Strat')
guitar.pickup: Seymour Duncan Custom SSL-1 bridge single-coil / Fender Custom Shop 69 neck pickup

amp.recommended: Hiwatt DR103 Custom 100W with WEM 4x12 Fane Speaker Cabinet

effects.distortion: Dallas Arbiter Silicon Fuzz Face / Electro-Harmonix 'Ram's Head' Big Muff
effects.other: Binson Echorec 2 Magnetic Disk Delay (~310ms multi-head echo), Colorsound Power Boost

beginner.title: Verse Chords & Rhythm Feel
steps: Learn the F#m, A, E, and Bm chord shapes
Practice the 120 BPM quarter-note groove with metronome
Understand the song's dynamic shifts between verse and chorus

intermediate.title: Chorus Major 7th Voicings & Transitions
steps: Master clean switching between Dmaj7 and Amaj7
Practice the descending turnaround: C#m to Bm to E
Learn the clean chord fills that lead into the solo

advanced.title: David Gilmour Solo Mastery
steps: Isolate the multi-step over-bends and verify pitch accuracy with a chromatic tuner
Master smooth, wide vocal wrist vibrato at the peak of full-step bends
Dial in tape delay and fuzz sustain to recreate Gilmour's singing tone

commonMistakes: Under-bending the 1.5-step bends on the G string, leaving notes flat and sour
Applying nervous, rapid finger vibrato instead of smooth, wide wrist-driven vibrato
Muting the shimmering high strings on the Dmaj7 chorus chord
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Pitch-bending calibration drills with chromatic tuner
10 min: Slow vibrato exercises on sustained whole notes
15 min: Solo phrasing and delay timing practice
10 min: Rhythm practice through the verse-chorus transitions
focusAreas: Exact pitch accuracy on 1-step and 1.5-step bends
Dynamic emotional storytelling throughout the guitar solo
metronomeWork: Practice the solo slowly at 80 BPM to lock in micro-timing
Increase to 100 BPM, ensuring bend releases are perfectly in time
Perform at album tempo of 120 BPM with backing track
